questions.question_text: In which of the following animals does the notochord persist throughout life?

options.text: Ascidia
Branchiostoma
Balanoglossus
Labeo

solution.concept: Fate of the notochord in different groups
solution.explanation: NCERT: in Cephalochordata (e.g., Branchiostoma) the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life. In vertebrates such as Labeo the notochord is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult.
steps: Cephalochordate → notochord head to tail, lifelong

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Hemichordata; phylum Chordata

Stopping substances from leaking across the tissue
Rapid transfer of ions and small molecules between adjoining cells
Production and secretion of collagen fibres

(c) During hibernation in the burrow, gaseous exchange takes place mainly through the lungs.

During aestivation and hibernation, gaseous exchange takes place through the skin.

questions.question_text: Suppose the collecting duct of a person's nephrons no longer allowed urea to pass into the medullary interstitium, while every other part of the kidney worked normally. Using NCERT's account, which effect is expected?

Glucose would begin to appear in the urine
The glomerular filtration rate would rise sharply
The ascending limb of Henle's loop would become permeable to water

solution.concept: Urea and the medullary osmolarity gradient
solution.explanation: NCERT: the collecting duct allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to keep up the osmolarity. Together with the counter-current mechanism, this maintains the concentration gradient in the medullary interstitium, and the gradient helps the easy passage of water from the collecting tubule, concentrating the filtrate. Without the urea contribution, the gradient – and hence urine concentration – would suffer.
steps: Urea into interstitium → keeps up medullary osmolarity
Gradient → water leaves the collecting duct → concentrated urine
No urea entry → weaker concentrating ability
solution.why_others_wrong: B depends on glucose reabsorption in the PCT; C depends on glomerular blood pressure; D is unrelated – the ascending limb stays impermeable to water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation – function of the tubules; mechanism of concentration of the filtrate
solution.final_answer: Option A: It would be harder to keep up the osmolarity of the medullary interstitium, so the ability to form concentrated urine would fall
